findings.text: red-team lens, medium: The gh backend reads the holder from the last comment on the issue that contains the zbuild-run-status magic marker, with no check that the comment came from the authenticated sidecar, so any GitHub user who can comment on the issue can displace the legitimate holder string. (plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh: "'[.[] | select(.body | contains("<!-- zbuild-run-status")) | .body] | last'"; happens when: On a public GitHub repository (or any repo where the attacker has comment access), the attacker posts a comment containing the string '<!-- zbuild-run-status run_id=x -->' and an arbitrary '<!-- zbuild-holder: PAYLOAD -->' line. Because jq's `last` selects the most recently posted matching comment, the attacker's PAYLOAD becomes the holder string extracted by _ccgl_read_holder, which is returned as the holder in claim_coordinator_claim's refusal JSON and printed to the operator's terminal on the next run that finds zbuild:claimed present.; fix: design; ACCEPTED IF: The holder string shown in the refusal message is taken only from comments that the authenticated sidecar process itself wrote, not from any comment any GitHub user can post to the issue.)
